title: Affine descent datum of fixed synchronized ordinary resolution towers
statement: Fix a totally ordered set $L$. Let $A$ be an ordinary Zariski resolution rule [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data], and let $B$ be a local smooth ordinary rule [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-resolution-descent-data]. Suppose the underlying labeled tower of $A(S)$ equals that of $B(S)$ for every input $S$ and every pair of embeddability witnesses. Let $R(S)$ be fixed global labeled ordinary towers [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule], each satisfying IsResolution, and suppose each $R(S)$ satisfies $A$.IsSynchronizedDescent: for every finite affine-cover total there is a unique full label-preserving cartesian comparison whose centers descend. Then there exists an affine descent datum $D$ [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-resolution-descent-data] whose local rule is exactly $B$ and whose underlying labeled global tower is exactly $R(S)$ for every $S$. In particular its specified full cover identifications [def-per-ordinary-tower-cartesian-map] satisfy the count and level-map cocycles for smooth maps between covers over the same input. This conclusion supplies no global smooth comparison or identity/composition/nondeletion theorem.

proof.text: For each S put D.tower S equal to the given R(S), with regularity and coherent-center proofs from IsResolution. Enumerate the finite index type of an AffineCover by Fin n. Identify its spectrum charts with their affine open ranges. Transport the component arrows and coproduct universal property along these isomorphisms; the total scheme and covering map stay unchanged. The covering and rational equations now form ResolutionAffineCover. Apply the supplied synchronized descent and change the output labeled tower by the assumed equality A=B. This gives the full CoverIdentification with all its center and label equalities.

proof.text: For a smooth v between two such cover totals over S, both total label lists equal the global list via the full cover identifications. Label preservation of B.comparison therefore makes its survivor embedding a bijection of equal finite ordered lists. Its count is the length-transport cast; this follows successively from count_zero and count_after, and handles singleton level sets too. This is precisely cocycle_count.

proof.text: After the count identification the composite through B.comparison and either full cover identification have the same initial map and extended ideals. Induct on stages to identify their level maps. At each blowup the center is invertible on the source by principalization, so uniqueness in the ordinary blowup universal property gives the same lift. An inserted unit stage is an identity and satisfies the same assertion. This proves cocycle_map with its specified transports. Enumerations have no effect by this uniqueness. Together with the fixed local rule and literal global-tower equations the constructions form the desired Datum.

lean.statement: theorem synchronizedResolution_descentDatum (L : Type w) [LinearOrder L] (A : OrdinaryZariskiResolutionRule.{u, w} L) (B : OrdinaryResolutionDescent.LocalRule.{u, w} L) (hAB : ∀ (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (eA : S.IsEmbeddable) (eB : OrdinaryResolutionDescent.Embeddable S), A.tower S eA = ⟨(B.tower S eB).tower, (B.tower S eB).labels⟩) (R : ∀ S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}, LabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme) (hR : ∀ S, (R S).IsResolution) (hdescent : ∀ S, A.IsSynchronizedDescent S (R S)) : ∃ D : OrdinaryResolutionDescent.Datum.{u, w} L, D.localRule = B ∧ ∀ S, (⟨(D.tower S).tower, (D.tower S).labels⟩ : LabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme) = R S
